earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlists (Lee 2006 SIL survei bahasa Emem; Smits & Voorhoeve 1994; Galis 1956; Voorhoeve 1975); no phonological description covering stress located.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [last modified 2024-06-25]. East Pauwasi River. New Guinea World (DokuWiki hosted at University of Zurich). Sources, historical phonology and correspondence tables for Zorop, Emem (Yuruf, Yambraf Dua) and Karkar.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on Emem stress or tone. 'Sources' lists only wordlists for Emem (Galis 1956; Voorhoeve 1971, 1975; Lee 2005; Lebold & Lee 2016) and, for the sister language only, 'Price (1981) Karkar stress'. The historical-phonology section reconstructs 11 proto-East-Pauwasi consonants and c. 11 vowels with reflex tables; Emem forms carry primary-stress marks copied from the SIL wordlists, i.e. wordlist-only stress data, no rule stated.

sources.citation: Lebold, Randy & Myung Young Lee. 2016. Survey Report on the Emem Language of Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2016-008. Dallas: SIL International. 47 pp. (published English version of Lee 2006 'Laporan survei pada bahasa Emem')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A sociolinguistic (Phase I rapid-appraisal) survey: no phonology, no mention of stress/accent/tone anywhere in the prose (a full-text search for stress/accent zero hits). Appendix B (the text layer) gives four IPA village wordlists (Yuruf, Umuaf, Yambraf Dua, Semografi) that carry primary-stress marks; my own tally of 320 polysyllabic tokens with one mark: 135 initial, 134 final, 51 medial, i.e. no fixed position visible, but the authors make no claim about it.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212. (p. 196 and fn. 19 on Eastern Pauwasi: Zorop [wfg], Emem [enr], Karkar-Yuri [yuj])
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Classification/documentation status only: 'the Eastern Pauwasi languages Zorop [wfg] and Emem [enr], on the Indonesian side, were not thought to be related to any of the neighboring languages.. However, Timothy Usher, after inspecting the wordlists (Whitehouse 2006), spotted the close relationship that in fact exists between Karkar-Yuri and the Eastern Pauwasi languages—Emem and Karkar-Yuri may even constitute a dialect continuum.' a full-text search for stress/accent the whole paper for stress/tone/accent: no hits relating to any Pauwasi language.
